The selected settings—Donchian length 3 and EMA 200—produced an equity curve that outperformed buy and hold with less volatility. However, the strategy made only 87 trades, limiting the reliability of those results and raising the risk of curve fitting. Two-hour results also appeared promising, but the passage recommends out-of-sample testing and an incubation period before considering live trading.

The passage presents a scalable method for making visible-light Fabry–Perot microcavities from buckled dielectric-coated silicon mirrors. Repeated oxidation and etching smooth the silicon before coating; suspended mirrors then buckle into concave shapes with radii of curvature from 0.9 to 21 mm. At 780 nm, the cavities achieved a maximum finesse of 0.89 million and a maximum quality factor of 2.3 billion. The authors also assembled compact cavities using glued mirror chips and describe potential uses in quantum optical interfaces, sensing, and laser stabilization.

Corning’s history of innovation spans specialty glass, cookware, optical fiber, display glass and other materials. After the telecommunications crash halved its revenue between 2001 and 2002 and led to more than 12,000 layoffs, the company continued investing in research. By 2008, its telecommunications sales and stock price had recovered, while display glass had become a major source of income.

Corning centrally manages long-term research while its business units handle product development, manufacturing and sales. Its Technology Council evaluates early-stage projects; the Growth and Strategy Council (GSC), led by the CEO, COO and CTO, guides more advanced projects and allocates resources across businesses. The GSC aims to maintain a balanced innovation portfolio through sustained investment and rigorous review.

Managers credited the GSC with supporting important diesel-filter and fiber-to-the-home opportunities, but some found its meetings too large. As Corning sought to launch new businesses more quickly, the council faced questions about its capacity to prioritize projects and assess unfamiliar markets and business models.

The S&P 500 Financial Services sector includes banks, investment firms, insurers and fintech companies; ETFs such as VFH and XLF track it. The passage names Berkshire Hathaway, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup and Goldman Sachs among its largest stocks as of July 2022. After an 85% decline from its 2007 peak, the sector consolidated. A backtested XLF strategy recorded 198 trades, a 1.05% average gain, a 73% win rate, a 21% maximum drawdown and a 2.25 profit factor. The passage notes the sector’s high volatility and correlation with the broader market.

Amazon is developing a home robot, codenamed Vesta, through its Lab126 hardware division. The company has increased hiring for the project and hopes to test robots in employees’ homes by year-end, with a possible consumer release in 2019, though plans could change. Its intended tasks remain unclear; prototypes use cameras and computer vision to navigate homes, and people familiar with the project suggest it could function as a mobile Alexa. The project is separate from Amazon’s warehouse robots.

San Miguel Pure Foods postponed its planned P100–150 billion share offering from the second quarter to the third or fourth quarter, citing other stock offerings and market volatility. The offering would raise the public float of the company formed by its merger with San Miguel Brewery and Ginebra San Miguel to meet the 15% minimum ownership requirement.

The passage describes a system for creating digital twins from data collected from physical assets and maintaining versions as those assets change. Users can simulate a current or earlier version, combine components from multiple versions into a hybrid model, bypass selected components, substitute alternatives, or supply overriding values for unsimulated portions. The system reports simulation results and allows users to revise parameters and rerun simulations.

Shopping malls are expanding across Nigeria, particularly in Lagos. The passage attributes their growth to demand for convenient, one-stop shopping and changing consumer habits. A mall executive says the expansion reflects investor confidence and creates jobs and tax revenue.

Exeter City lost 1-0 at league leaders Luton Town to Harry Cornick’s deflected strike. Manager Paul Tisdale said Luton deserved the win but praised Exeter’s performance despite six defensive absences and 20-year-old Jordan Storey making his first league start. He disputed the decision to rule out Liam McAlinden’s late equaliser and said Exeter could approach their next match against Wycombe Wanderers with confidence.

Messaging apps are expanding beyond chat into services that encourage user engagement. WeChat already offers services including food ordering, games and dating. In India, WhatsApp has about 94% reach and is adding payments after introducing voice and video calls. The passage also discusses content and gaming as ways to increase engagement, Hike’s efforts to compete, and the growing influence of large conglomerate-backed companies on India’s internet.

At reset de-assertion, BTMODE pin states are latched into CONTROL_STATUS. BTMODE[4:0] sets the boot sequence; [15:11] configures GPMC CS0; [9:8] selects Ethernet PHY mode for EMAC boot; and [10] selects GPMC muxing for XIP boot. Reserved [7:5] should be pulled down.

At Apple’s March 10, 2015 annual meeting, shareholders elected seven directors and approved Ernst & Young as the 2015 auditor, executive compensation, and an increase of 50 million shares authorized under the Employee Stock Purchase Plan. Shareholder proposals for a risk report and proxy access were rejected.

The passage describes a network security appliance with a local touch-screen interface for managing packet-filtering rules when attacks disrupt remote access. It can prioritize the interface during denial-of-service attacks, allowing an administrator to block traffic or change rules without rebooting or disconnecting the appliance. It can also hold packets from unrecognized devices until a user authorizes them locally. Other described methods use spatial indexing to speed rule matching and distribute mandatory and selected potential-threat rules across appliances to limit resource use.

Environment and Climate Change Canada found that none of the phthalates it reviewed posed a human health risk, though one needs further study for environmental risk. Environmental Defence criticized the finding, citing different European conclusions and rules requiring manufacturers to prove safety. The government said it would respond to proposed changes to Canada’s chemicals law by June 2018.

The passage argues that requiring particular standardized tests in school choice programs, graduation rules, and college admissions can narrow instruction and limit educational diversity. It cites studies linking high-stakes tests to changes in curriculum and teaching, and criticizes the SAT and other exams for declining rigor. Rather than banning tests, it recommends that states offer multiple assessments for school choice programs, graduation, public college admissions, and scholarships. It presents the Classic Learning Test as one alternative and notes that Arkansas and Florida already permit some testing choices.

The Supreme Court will hear arguments in a challenge to Colorado’s 2019 law barring licensed mental health professionals from providing conversion therapy to minors. Counselor Kaley Chiles argues that applying the ban to her talk therapy restricts speech based on its message and should face strict constitutional scrutiny. Colorado says the law regulates an unsafe and ineffective treatment, not speech, and protects minors while allowing other discussions about sexual orientation and gender identity. Lower courts declined to block enforcement against Chiles, applying the less demanding rational-basis test. The federal government supports sending the case back for review under strict scrutiny.

Businesses from across the south coast gathered at Brighton’s Grand Hotel for the seventh Johnston Press South Business Awards, presented by Nick Wallis. Chichester’s Guardian Angel Carers won Large Business of the Year and the top prize, Overall Business of the Year. Other winners included The Olive and Vine for Place to Eat or Drink, Brandon Relph of Go Creative for Young Achiever, Southsea Bathing Hut for Retailer of the Year, and Chichester’s Talks at 6 for Outstanding Contribution to the Community.

In a suit over automobile damage at a street intersection, the court affirmed a verdict for the defendants. The jury instructions adequately addressed the plaintiff’s allegations, including failure to sound a horn. Without allegations or special requests, the court was not required to instruct on right of way or reduced speed. The evidence supported a comparative-negligence instruction and the defendants’ verdict; any error concerning the measure of damages was harmless.

A Canadian Society of Palliative Care Physicians report concludes that expanding palliative care across Canada could improve patient care while reducing health costs. Cited studies found that hospital-based palliative care saves about $7,000–$8,000 per patient compared with usual acute care, while outpatient services save about 30%. The report also cites projected savings from expanding home-based care in Ontario and estimates that residential hospices save about $600 per day compared with acute care. The society recommends improving access to a mix of palliative care and hospice services and evaluating their quality and benefits.

AMP chairman David Murray argued that increasingly prescriptive ASX governance guidelines discourage better models and have contributed to declining standards and trust in the financial sector. He urged institutions to overhaul their governance practices.

The Central Bank of Nigeria introduced Form X to ease foreign-exchange applications for SMEs with needs of $10,000 or less. Applicants must submit the form, an application letter, a beneficiary invoice and bank wire transfer documentation.

Gardaí appealed for information about the murder of 18-year-old Cameron Reilly in Dunleer, particularly his missing iPhone, which may contain relevant messages. Separately, officers arrested two people after intercepting a semi-automatic shotgun handover in west Dublin. Follow-up searches found heroin, cocaine and cash.

Breast lumps can vary in size and texture and may occur in the breast or armpit. Other warning signs include swelling, skin dimpling, nipple changes, discharge, rashes and unexplained pain. The passage advises checking breasts regularly to learn what is normal and seeking medical advice about unfamiliar changes. Breast cancer can also affect men. Screening may detect cancer when no lump is noticed, and early diagnosis can make treatment more effective.

The passage describes techniques for improving fast-forward and rewind during streamed video playback. A client buffers continuous video for normal playback while separately downloading selected frames, often key frames, from portions not fully buffered. It uses those frames for faster-than-real-time playback without downloading every intervening frame, then can retrieve missing frames if needed for normal playback. Frame selection, quality, and buffering may adapt to playback speed and network performance. An optional proxy server can provide frame indexes and other metadata when a streaming server does not.

NVIDIA appointed Donald F. Robertson Jr. vice president, chief accounting officer and principal accounting officer, effective June 17, 2019. He succeeds Michael Byron, who moves to a new finance role. Robertson’s offer includes a $650,000 annual salary, a $600,000 sign-on bonus and 15,000 restricted stock units.

A 167-million-year-old lizard fossil found on Scotland’s Isle of Skye combines snake-like jaws and curved teeth with a short body, limbs and gecko-like features. Named *Breugnathair elgolensis*, it belongs to a newly defined group of extinct predatory squamates, Parviraptoridae. The fossil shows that traits previously attributed to separate animals occurred together. Researchers cannot yet determine whether it was related to snake ancestors or independently evolved snake-like features.

SPYR announced that shareholders of record on May 19, 2017, would receive one share in a planned restaurant-division spin-off for each SPYR share held. The new company plans to pursue licensing or franchising of the Eat at Joe’s name and the manufacture and distribution of branded foods. SPYR said the spin-off would seek separate public trading status after its formation. The article discusses hypothetical share values but does not establish a future price. Its publisher, Stock Market Media Group, disclosed a compensation agreement with SPYR that included a $5,000 monthly fee and 250,000 restricted shares.

Travis Haydon, 20, was sentenced to 18 months in a young offender institution after stabbing Liam Brown in the stomach during a pub argument over a spilt drink in Plymouth. Brown was treated for a puncture wound and kept in hospital overnight; he was not thought to have suffered lasting damage. Haydon pleaded guilty to assault causing actual bodily harm, carrying a knife in public and possessing cannabis. He also admitted breaching a suspended sentence for affray.

The A100 GPU has 40 MB of L2 cache, 6.7 times the V100’s capacity. Its two partitions improve memory access and provide 2.3 times the V100’s L2 bandwidth. The larger cache can benefit workloads limited by DRAM bandwidth. Programmers can control cache residency, while L2 compression can improve DRAM read/write and L2 read bandwidth by up to four times.

The passage describes features and design guidance for TI’s MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers. It covers the RTC_B clock and alarms, independent and windowed watchdogs, general-purpose and advanced timers, analog connections, I/O control, serial-wire debugging, and UART or I2C bootloader programming. It also identifies read-only factory constants and recommends specific decoupling, reset, oscillator, and VCORE components for typical applications. Later sections list development tools and documentation, distinguish experimental from production devices, summarize revisions made in April 2025, and provide packaging information and TI disclaimers.
Evo 1 and Evo 2 designed bacteriophage genomes; some outperformed a studied strain in laboratory dishes.

DoorDash unveiled Dot, a nearly five-foot-tall delivery robot intended for sidewalks, roads, and bike lanes as part of a delivery model combining people and autonomous vehicles. The discussion examines technical obstacles, bike-lane access, regulations, and the human work still needed to support robot deliveries. It also notes that some companies have scaled back delivery-robot projects, while others continue testing them in more predictable settings such as college campuses.

Chicago expects large crowds for the marathon, a Cubs playoff game and a Bears game, posing a major security challenge after the Las Vegas mass shooting. Officials say they have reviewed security plans, including potential threats from nearby high-rises. Police will deploy 1,000 additional officers for the marathon and increase undercover patrols. Existing measures include bag checks and restricted access to the race’s start and finish areas. Mayor Rahm Emanuel said he is confident the events are secure. Some runners said the Las Vegas attack raised concerns but did not change their plans to compete.

Saudi Aramco plans to change the benchmark for its long-term crude sales to Asia from October, trade sources said. Its official selling prices will use an equal-weighted average of DME Oman futures and Platts-assessed Dubai cash prices, replacing Platts assessments of both Oman and Dubai. The change could increase trading in DME Oman futures and related hedging instruments. It remains unclear whether other Middle Eastern producers will follow.

The Florida appellate court reversed the denial of Genel Altimeaux’s unemployment benefits. The finding that he voluntarily quit relied on testimony from a hearing he had not been notified of and at which he could not cross-examine the witness. At a second hearing, no witness testified to hearing Altimeaux quit, and Altimeaux denied doing so. The court directed that his unemployment award be reinstated.

Some Highland Park High School parents question the transparency of District 113’s principal search and why only two parents serve on its 18-member stakeholder interview committee. A search firm is screening candidates to replace Tom Koulentes, who leaves June 30. District administrators plan to narrow the field before the committee interviews finalists April 25. Superintendent Christopher Dignam says the process matches one used at Deerfield High School.

The speaker welcomes visiting chiefs and urges peace, promising to respect agreed boundaries and protect their lands from encroachment. Responding to their request to sell land to pay merchant debts, he expresses interest in land along the Mississippi but says representatives must negotiate the boundary on site. He says earlier land sold to the English was paid for and that any unpaid debt would belong to the English. He encourages farming and weaving, clarifies that past gifts and a store on their land require no land payment, and promises arrangements for the chiefs’ travels and return home.

Pin and Pull is a perimeter run that uses down blocks to create favorable angles and pulling linemen as lead blockers. Its flexibility lets blockers adjust to the defensive front and the tailback run from the C-gap to the sideline. It requires guards who can pull and run, and works best with a speedy tailback. Unlike Buck Sweep, it does not require a simultaneous inside run threat. The passage outlines blocking assignments against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts and two toss variations.

Researchers fitted greater noctule bats with sensors and microphones to study how they hunt at night. Of 611 recorded hunting events, two involved bats pursuing migrating songbirds from high altitude. One bird escaped; recordings of the other captured distress calls followed by a 23-minute in-flight meal. The findings provide evidence that greater noctules catch and eat birds in flight.

Former Nepali prime minister K.P. Oli won his parliamentary seat, and his Communist UML party and Maoist allies were on course for a majority as votes were counted. Oli has pledged a full five-year government and infrastructure projects to create jobs. Final results are expected in about a week.

Verizon and AST SpaceMobile announced a commercial agreement to provide space-based cellular broadband across the continental US. The author maintains a “strong buy” rating on Verizon, citing modest long-term benefits from the partnership and a favorable financial outlook. The author rates AST SpaceMobile a “sell,” citing dilution, minimal revenue and a high valuation despite its operational milestones and partnerships.

Brock University researchers found that rosemary extract inhibited the growth and spread of cultured lung cancer cells, blocked the Akt signalling pathway and increased programmed cell death. They are investigating which components cause these effects. Lead researcher Evangelina Tsiani cautioned that it is too soon to recommend eating rosemary to prevent or stop lung cancer.

The article says gold rallied as the U.S. Dollar Index fell, but silver and mining stocks showed little response. It interprets miners’ weakness as a bearish signal for precious metals and expects the dollar to strengthen. It also argues that recent stock-market declines point to further losses. The page includes advertisements, reader comments and trading-risk disclosures.

A January 2002 collection of reports examines Enron’s collapse. Enron claimed $110.9 million in profits from its Braveheart partnership tied to a short-lived Blockbuster video venture, then reversed those gains. Reports describe scrutiny of Enron’s partnerships, board oversight and Arthur Andersen’s auditing and destruction of documents. Investigations also raised questions about political contacts and SEC Chairman Harvey Pitt’s ties to the accounting industry. Other reports cover employees’ retirement losses, disruption to European energy trading and American Electric Power’s acquisition of Enron Nordic Energy.

BioNTech published a slide deck for its InstaDeep special call. The passage also includes a Seeking Alpha transcripts-team note, related article headlines, and chart ranges for September 26–October 1, 2025.

COTUTOR is an AI-assisted education model that combines student learning signals, knowledge tracing, signal processing, and convex optimization to personalize feedback and allocate learning resources. It updates mastery estimates from interactions such as programming submissions and uses an AI chatbot to provide reminders, answer questions, and recommend materials. A case study formulates resource allocation across educational sessions as an optimization problem, accounting for resource dependencies and student sentiment. The paper reports that dataset benchmarks and a controlled classroom study found improved performance and learning outcomes compared with previous methods.

The passage describes NVIDIA GA10x Ampere GPUs and related products. GDDR6X provides up to 936 GB/sec of peak memory bandwidth, while second-generation RT Cores and third-generation Tensor Cores improve ray tracing and AI performance. RTX IO, used with Microsoft DirectStorage, moves game-asset decompression to the GPU to reduce CPU demands and accelerate loading. The passage also covers the A40 and RTX A6000 for data-center and workstation workloads, high-resolution display support, AV1 hardware decoding, and NVENC video encoding. Product notes describe the RTX 3090 and 3070, plus error detection and replay for GDDR6X memory overclocking. NVIDIA concludes with specifications, testing notes, and legal limitations.

The 32-mile M4 stretch between London and Theale will become a four-lane smart motorway, costing up to £862.4m and due for completion by March 2022. The RAC raised concerns about the lack of a hard shoulder.

A November 26 news roundup covers Enron’s financial troubles and proposed acquisition by Dynegy. Enron sought up to $1 billion from investors while Dynegy reviewed its finances; a sharp share-price decline raised questions about the deal’s terms and completion. Articles also discuss Enron’s accounting restatements, broader concerns about inconsistent earnings reporting, potential antitrust scrutiny of the merger, and Enron’s stake in India’s Dabhol power project.

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said AI is a lasting technology that businesses should use, but warned that some AI-related asset prices are in “bubble territory.” He distinguished JPMorgan’s established AI applications, including fraud prevention, from generative AI, whose efficiency gains he said are harder to measure. Dimon urged leaders to invest in training and prepare for job losses through measures such as retraining or income support, rather than ignore the disruption.

Jane Goodall, who died at 91, preserved skeletons of chimpanzees she had studied at Tanzania’s Gombe National Park. Because researchers knew each chimp’s history, the collection offered a way to investigate how life experiences shape bones. In a 1990 interview, Goodall cautioned that its implications for understanding ancient hominids remained unknown. Flo’s skeleton, for example, showed why bone size can be a poor guide to body weight. Goodall explained her practice simply: field researchers “shouldn’t waste anything.”

A Business Insider reporter spent one night in the Aurora Suite at Miami’s former Versace Mansion, paying $864 for the cheapest available room. Attentive staff and largely empty guest areas made the stay feel private. The reporter enjoyed the spacious suite, ornate shower, gold-tiled pool, rooftop views, and complimentary breakfast.

Gold could reach $1,400 an ounce by year-end, according to VTB Capital’s Evgeny Ananiev, amid U.S.–North Korea tensions and stronger demand from China and India. Metals Focus analyst Chirag Sheth also expects $1,400, but within six to nine months. Prices have risen 12 percent this year; subdued U.S. inflation and a softer Federal Reserve stance have added support. Sheth expects Indian jewelry consumption and imports to grow, while Chinese gold-bar demand rose by more than half in the first six months of the year.

Asian shares were mostly lower Wednesday after a late sell-off ended a three-day winning streak for U.S. stocks. Major indexes fell in Japan, China, Hong Kong, South Korea and Australia, while shares rose in Southeast Asia and Taiwan. Investors faced impending U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports and expected Chinese retaliation. Comments from China’s central bank governor about the yuan and financial stability helped reassure investors. Oil prices rose, while the dollar weakened against the yen.

The Student Finance Board denied additional funding for the Association of Students for Africa’s Akwaaba Banquet and funding for the Unified Greek Council’s Stroll for a Cure, citing high costs per student. It tabled a request for A Taste of South America over concerns about charitable-event rules and food costs. The board funded three dance-centered events—AirBand, Mystique of the East and Once Upon A Rock Step—but tabled a dance-floor rental for the latter because of its cost. It also funded its Summer Training Retreat.

Researchers tested poplar trees fortified with a TCE-degrading microbe at a contaminated Superfund research area in California. After three years, treated trees were healthier than untreated trees and had much less TCE in their trunks. Groundwater downstream from the test site also had lower TCE levels than groundwater up-gradient. The researchers say the approach could offer a more effective, lower-cost way to clean contaminated sites.

The passage describes multi-camera systems for imaging faint objects using cameras that may be insufficient individually. In a common field array, software aligns and combines images from cameras viewing the same region to improve signal-to-noise ratio. Hybrid arrays stitch together images from overlapping camera groups to widen the field of view. Adaptive arrays initially survey a wider area, then redirect cameras toward a detected target to improve its image. The passage also describes camera calibration and a process for detecting object streaks, estimating orbits, and checking a catalog to identify uncorrelated targets.

Reports citing anonymous U.S. officials say Russian intelligence officials repeatedly contacted Trump campaign staff during the election. U.S. agencies intercepted the communications and are investigating their purpose, but officials said they have not found proof of collusion. Trump and the Kremlin dismissed the reports. The FBI is investigating contacts between Trump aides and Russia, and a Senate committee is examining alleged Russian election interference. Republican Rep. Mike Johnson opposed an independent investigation and urged scrutiny of intelligence leaks. The reports follow the departures of Michael Flynn, Paul Manafort and Carter Page amid questions about their Russia contacts; Manafort denied involvement with Putin’s government.

After Iraq declared victory over Islamic State, Shi’ite cleric Moqtada al-Sadr said his followers would hand over their weapons if they received jobs or joined official forces and the government supported families of fighters killed in the war.

The passage describes deploying three Redis cache shards with a Kubernetes StatefulSet, giving them DNS names through a Service, and configuring twemproxy to route to the shards. A ConfigMap provides the proxy configuration to an ambassador pod, which serves Redis on localhost:6379 for the application.

A security guard collapsed and died at Rourkela’s Padmanava College of Engineering a week after assistant professor Jharna Dalei’s suicide. Police said the deaths were unrelated and registered an abetment case against an absconding faculty member.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2020, reports third-quarter revenue of $8.77 billion, up from $6.30 billion a year earlier, and net income attributable to common stockholders of $331 million, up from $143 million. For the first nine months, revenue was $20.79 billion and net income attributable to common stockholders was $451 million, compared with a $967 million loss in 2019. Cash and cash equivalents reached $14.53 billion. Tesla reported a five-for-one stock split and two 2020 stock offerings. It also described COVID-19-related disruptions, although all manufacturing facilities had resumed operations.

Researchers shock-compressed natural zircon crystals to 13.6 and 51.3 GPa to examine phase changes and trace elements. At 13.6 GPa, zircon remained the dominant phase despite extensive fracturing. At 51.3 GPa, it transformed largely to reidite, with minor residual zircon. Luminescence images revealed small regions enriched in rare-earth-element signals, some associated with planar defects. Because segregation occurred without prolonged annealing, the authors propose that the zircon–reidite transition may rapidly mobilize trace elements. They also suggest that fracturing could facilitate their release during later interaction with fluid or melt.

The White House blocked congressionally approved funding for the federal council overseeing inspectors general, effectively shuttering it Tuesday night. Two senators called for the funds’ immediate release.

The passage describes a scanning ladar transmitter designed to improve its gaze on selected regions. An optical field splitter/inverter redirects faster portions of a scan toward the edges, allowing more time to scan central regions. Periodic phase drift in a Lissajous scan can reduce gaps in selected regions. An ellipsoidal reflector reimages the beam between two scanning mirrors, enabling a more compact assembly with smaller, closely spaced mirrors.

A June 5 news roundup covers California’s energy crisis, including disputes over wholesale price limits, natural gas prices and possible market manipulation. Power plants were returning from maintenance and electricity use had fallen, but observers still expected summer blackouts. Other reports describe PG&E’s bankruptcy and legal challenges, proposed utility rate increases, new power contracts, and a state Senate inquiry seeking energy companies’ pricing records.

Microsoft’s April 27, 2021 Form 8-K reports that it issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2021. The release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1; the filing does not include the results themselves.

Party-list Rep. Lito Atienza has filed a bill to replace the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority with a Metro Manila government led by an elected governor. The bill also calls for an elected vice governor and council. Atienza argues that the MMDA’s appointed chairman lacks accountability and that an elected government could implement a development master plan addressing traffic, flooding, garbage and other problems.

The Citi Simplicity® Card offers 0% introductory APR for 21 months on balance transfers and 12 months on purchases. Afterward, a variable APR of 17.99%–28.74% applies. Transfers made within four months incur a 3% fee (minimum $5); later transfers incur a 5% fee (minimum $5). The card has no annual fee, late fees, or penalty rate. The recommended credit score is 670–850, but approval is not guaranteed. Motley Fool Money receives compensation from partners, including Citi, but says this does not influence its ratings.

This December 31, 2001, collection of business articles focuses on Enron’s bankruptcy and its effects on bandwidth trading, energy companies, creditors, investors and regulatory scrutiny. Other articles examine how large write-offs and credit markets can signal financial distress, warn against unrealistic stock-growth expectations, and report concerns about 401(k) investments concentrated in company stock. The collection also covers disputed executive bonuses at bankrupt Polaroid, delayed U.S. power-plant projects, California’s power crisis, and American Electric Power’s purchase of an Enron wind project.

Ten-man Manchester City moved up to third with a 2-1 win over Burnley. Fernandinho was sent off before half-time for a two-footed challenge and faces a four-match ban. Gael Clichy and substitute Sergio Aguero scored after the break; Ben Mee replied, but Burnley could not equalise.

Scientists estimate a 1-in-2,700 chance that asteroid Bennu will strike Earth in September 2135. NASA researchers have studied a theoretical response called HAMMER, which could deflect Bennu with an impactor or a nuclear device. No such mission is being built; the study aims to improve preparations for future threats. Bennu’s well-studied shape makes it useful for testing deflection calculations, while NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft will map the asteroid, analyze its composition and return a sample to Earth.

The Consumer Mortgage Coalition urged the Treasury Department to let mortgage lenders use a federal employment database to verify applicants’ income, citing problems with the IRS system that could delay spring mortgage closings. It said access would require consumer consent and also called for funding to upgrade the IRS system.

Eric Fung moved from California to Tokyo to build Colega AI, a US-registered startup with a team spread across Asia. He sought a fresh start after finding Bay Area living costs too high and saw Japan’s many small businesses as a promising market. A local partner helps him navigate language and cultural barriers. Fung is adjusting to Japanese work culture, while he and his wife appreciate Tokyo’s safety, convenience, and lower housing costs.

Nifty’s long/short stop levels are 10,050/10,200; Bank Nifty’s are 24,225/24,450. Bank Nifty’s trend remains negative, though Monday short-covering is possible. The passage recommends shorting Tata Steel and Ambuja Cements and buying PowerGrid.

CompareCards compares credit cards with introductory 0% APR periods, cash-back or travel rewards, and sign-up bonuses. The listed offers vary in duration, balance-transfer fees, and rates after the introductory period. The site says it receives compensation from listed companies but that this does not influence its ratings or reviews.

A study of the 2014–2016 West African Ebola epidemic found that 3 percent of patients caused about 61 percent of infections in others. Transmission was limited after patients reached hospitals, while people who remained at home and traditional funeral practices contributed to the spread. The very young and very old were more likely to be superspreaders, the researchers found. The epidemic infected more than 28,000 people and killed at least 11,000; safe burials and rapid hospitalization helped stop it.

The author argues that Sirius XM’s low-cost fixed-rate debt, share buybacks and planned satellite spending cuts support strong cash flow. The passage projects roughly 20% more free cash flow by 2026 and potential 2–3× upside based on a discounted cash flow analysis. The author holds a long position in SIRI.
The Cubs’ Korean corn dog tops new 2025 ballpark foods. ESPN2 will air the Savannah Bananas selection show Oct. 9.

The automated fare collection market was valued at $4.81 billion in 2016 and is projected to reach $12.81 billion by 2024. These systems automate public-transit ticketing and can reduce queues and manual errors while improving transaction security. Growth is attributed to these benefits and new technologies, while limited awareness and smart-card use may restrain it. The market is segmented by component, application, technology and geography.

Bayhorse Silver increased its proposed non-brokered private placement to 3 million units at C$0.10 each, for C$300,000, subject to TSX Venture Exchange approval. Each unit includes a share and half a warrant. Proceeds will support equipment purchases, mine operations, and general and administrative costs.

The passage describes proposed methods for transmitting small uplink data in New Radio while a user equipment remains RRC idle or inactive. A base station can broadcast contention-based resources for a configured-grant uplink channel, potentially with non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) parameters. The passage also describes jointly encoding user-specific reference bits with data to generate preambles or demodulation reference signals, aiming to reduce sequence collisions and support user detection and decoding. Additional configurations address resource allocation, timing, interference and reception responses.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture improves FP32 processing, ray tracing and AI performance over Turing. Its second-generation RT Cores support concurrent ray tracing and graphics or compute work, and accelerate ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32, BF16 and structured sparsity, supporting AI training, denoising and DLSS. Other features include GDDR6X memory, larger caches, PCIe Gen 4, NVLink and RTX IO, which moves game-asset decompression work from the CPU to the GPU. The architecture also supports high-resolution displays, AV1 hardware decoding and hardware video encoding. The passage describes GeForce RTX 30-series cards alongside the RTX A6000 workstation GPU and A40 data-center GPU, including their rendering, compute, virtualization and memory-scaling capabilities.

The Massachusetts House and Senate passed bills providing $15 million to school districts educating students who arrived from Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. More than 2,300 students have arrived since September, but districts have received no additional aid under the existing formula. The chambers must resolve minor differences before sending the bill to Governor Baker.

Police are appealing for witnesses after a father was allegedly spat at, punched and kicked by two men in Coed Bach Park, Pontarddulais, on 29 June. The attack reportedly followed his request that a moped rider take more care around children. His children witnessed the incident.

The Tax Court upheld a proposed levy to collect Robert Poindexter’s unpaid 1994 and 1996 income taxes. Although he was entitled to challenge the liabilities reported on his own returns, he did not identify specific errors or provide facts supporting his claims. The court granted summary judgment for the Commissioner.

Agents Mutual plans to float OnTheMarket.com on London’s Alternative Investment Market and raise £50 million to challenge Rightmove and Zoopla. Britain’s third-largest online property site intends to invest in marketing, sales, customer relations and technology. Analyst George Salmon said overtaking the leading portals remains a significant challenge. Earlier this year, OnTheMarket won a case upholding its rule limiting agents to one additional rival listing site.

The Ninth Circuit affirmed tax deficiencies against a corporation operating in American Samoa. Payments from its parent were deposited in its Honolulu bank account and therefore received within the United States, making them taxable under section 931(b) despite the corporation’s eligibility for the section 931(a) exclusion.

The insured sought coverage for cash and payroll checks stolen from his safe. His only written record was a total of $2,922, with no details identifying the checks; he later recovered $182 by recalling two of them. The court held that the records did not allow the insurers to accurately determine the loss or pursue payment on the remaining checks. It reversed the judgment and ordered the complaint dismissed.

After passing an online “Jeopardy!” test, John Kizer reflects on how people recall long-forgotten facts. He says neuroscience still lacks a consensus on how memories are stored. Experiments have suggested both widespread and localized memory storage, while recent snail research suggests RNA may transfer memories. Kizer recalls struggling to replicate earlier flatworm experiments that also linked RNA to memory. He emphasizes that scientific findings can be difficult to establish and that understanding memory loss would have practical importance for an aging population.

Acting CDC director Jim O’Neill approved recommendations allowing people over 6 months old to receive an updated Covid-19 shot after discussing its risks and benefits with a provider. The approval preserves insurance coverage and lets states order doses for children in the Vaccines for Children program, though prescription requirements remain unclear. O’Neill also approved separate MMR and chickenpox shots for children under 4.

The passage evaluates variance reduction and population control methods for time-dependent Monte Carlo neutron transport simulations. Tests in Shift and MC/DC show that Cooper-Larsen weight windows combined with uniform combing substantially improve efficiency, with time-dependent windows outperforming static ones. Weight windows combined with weight-based combing caused excessive particle splitting and memory failures, while implicit capture performed poorly with uniform combing. FW-CADIS provided modest gains in a pulsed-slab test. The results highlight the importance of choosing compatible methods.

The article argues that language education should emphasize how languages connect people, particularly amid declining U.S. enrollments. It proposes fostering “imagined communities” through plausible tasks in which students picture themselves using a target language in everyday situations, such as finding housing or navigating a city. Instructors can adapt these tasks across educational levels, using authentic materials, student choice, and support as needed. A study in eighth-grade German classrooms reported deeper cultural learning and stronger feelings of connection to target-language speakers.

The National Endowment for the Humanities and First Nations Development Institute will each contribute about $2 million to fund Native language education in tribal communities. The competitive grants will prioritize working immersion programs and language retention or restoration efforts. About 15 programs are expected to receive funding each year.

A May 3, 2001 news digest covers a proposed Enron plant in Florida, California’s electricity costs and debate over refusing high-priced power, and a payment dispute involving Enron’s Dabhol project in India. Allegheny Energy bought three gas-fired plants totaling 1,710 megawatts from an Enron unit, while Enron Wind agreed to supply turbines for projects in Germany and Spain. Other reports discuss power-trading expansion, credit derivatives, utility forecasts and Scottish Power’s restructuring plans.

After Rep. Steve Scalise and three others were shot at a congressional baseball practice, Rep. Garret Graves said divisive rhetoric and misinformation had contributed to an unhealthy political climate. Scalise was in critical condition. Police had not stated a motive, though the shooter had expressed anti-Republican views and volunteered for Bernie Sanders’s campaign. Sanders condemned the violence, and President Donald Trump called for unity.

The speaker felt energized despite extensive power-play and penalty-killing time. They credited the team’s four scoring lines and said both teams defended well on penalties. After discussing the need to stay composed, the team found an opening, and the speaker got a shot through to Irbe.

The passage describes genetically modified host cells and cell-free methods for producing cannabinoids, their precursors, and derivatives. It focuses on a newly identified geranyltransferase, CsPT4, that converts geranyl pyrophosphate and olivetolic acid into cannabigerolic acid at least ten times more effectively than a previously identified Cannabis enzyme. A version lacking its first 76 amino acids retains similar activity. Additional enzymes can supply precursors or convert cannabigerolic acid into compounds including cannabidiolic acid and tetrahydrocannabinolic acid. The disclosure also covers the enzymes, their encoding nucleic acids and vectors, and methods for culturing modified cells and recovering the products.

Amazon’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2019, reports third-quarter net sales of $70.0 billion, up from $56.6 billion a year earlier, while net income fell from $2.9 billion to $2.1 billion. For the first nine months of 2019, net sales rose to $193.1 billion and net income to $8.3 billion. AWS sales reached $9.0 billion in the third quarter. At September 30, total assets were $199.1 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $43.4 billion.

An Ilorin Magistrates’ Court remanded herdsmen Shehu Abubakar and Abdulkareem Maikudi over the alleged killing of their colleague, Musa Kareem, after a dispute over a cell phone. Police said the accused admitted beating him with sticks. The prosecutor said the investigation was ongoing, and the court adjourned the case until July 12.

Most federal judges who responded to a New York Times survey criticized the Supreme Court’s emergency docket decisions involving Trump administration policies. Of 65 respondents, 47 disagreed that the Court had used the docket appropriately, and 48 said lower courts lacked sufficient guidance. Among 54 who answered a separate question, 42 said the orders harmed public perception of the judiciary. The newspaper noted that respondents may not represent all federal judges; a published critique argued that dissatisfied judges may have been more likely to respond.

Energy Central’s January 15, 2002, daily edition compiles electric power, gas and utility-stock news. Top stories cover National Grid’s proposed Niagara Mohawk takeover, officials’ calls with Enron, UBS’s purchase of Enron’s trading business, and utility stranded-cost bonds. Other articles address Enron investigations, electricity deregulation, California’s energy market, power projects, renewable energy and international utility developments.

The court affirmed the denial of Michael Moss’s unemployment benefits. The Board found that he resigned in lieu of discharge after pulling a box cutter on his supervisor, constituting disqualifying misconduct. His denial presented a credibility issue for the Board.

Nigeria launched its 2018–2022 National Cancer Control Plan to improve access to cancer diagnosis, treatment and medicines. At the launch, BIO Ventures for Global Health described its AAI partnership with Nigeria, including hospital needs assessments intended to guide sustainable access to cancer treatments.

JPMorgan downgraded Valero from Overweight to Neutral while raising its price target from $75 to $78. Analysts said improved returns and capital discipline were already reflected in the stock, while a further valuation increase could take time. They expect free cash flow to cover the dividend in a downside scenario, though buybacks could stop, and estimate 6% total return potential.

A retrospective study of 1,918 intensive care patients with intracerebral hemorrhage found that higher resting heart rate was associated with greater all-cause mortality at 30 days, 90 days and one year. The association was significant above 78.5 beats per minute; analyses identified 90.3 beats per minute as a reference point above which mortality risk increased. The authors propose resting heart rate as a potential risk-stratification measure but note limitations and call for further research.

President Trump’s pardon of Scooter Libby, following an FBI raid on his lawyer Michael Cohen, renewed debate over whether he might use pardons in connection with the Mueller investigation. The White House said Libby’s pardon corrected an injustice; critics said it could signal support for associates under investigation. The White House denied sending such a message and did not rule out a future pardon for Cohen.

Legal scholars agree that presidential pardon power is broad but disagree on whether a pardon issued for a corrupt purpose—or a self-pardon—would be valid. Pardons do not prevent impeachment. Democrats have proposed federal disclosure requirements and a change to New York law to limit the effects of potentially strategic pardons. Analysts also note that a pardoned person could be compelled to testify about the pardoned crime.

The passage introduces mechanical, packaging, and orderable information for designated TI devices, including tape dimensions and fabrication notes. The information may change without notice. TI provides its technical resources “as is,” disclaims warranties, and states that developers are responsible for selecting products, validating applications, and meeting applicable requirements.

Edinburgh has experienced more haar than usual this spring. The Met Office attributes it to reduced temperature contrasts across the Atlantic, which have weakened the jet stream and allowed persistent easterly winds to replace the usual westerlies.

Purdue University ended its GEAR UP college-prep program for more than 13,000 low-income Indiana students after the Trump administration canceled a $34.9 million grant. The Education Department cited concerns about the grant application’s DEI provisions. Purdue did not appeal.

The lecture explains how hedonic pricing models use housing transactions to estimate what buyers and tenants pay for building and neighborhood attributes, including green certification, transit access, parks, and schools. Regression separates these attributes’ contributions to price, but estimates can be biased when green buildings differ from comparison buildings in other ways. The lecturer discusses omitted variables, reverse causality, selection bias, and methods for making more comparable comparisons, including geographic matching and randomized trials. Examples show how estimated premiums can inform building, park, and transit investments. The lecture also notes that improvements such as New York’s High Line can raise property values while contributing to environmental gentrification.
The ID Buzz remains unapproved for production but could arrive around 2025. The ID targets Golf buyers, while the all-wheel-drive Crozz may suit a broader U.S. launch.

DWH Deutsche Werte Holding AG moved to the Vienna Stock Exchange’s mid market segment on 23 April 2018, committing to increased transparency. The exchange also anticipates legal changes that would let Austrian companies trade bearer shares on the Third Market again.

The Supreme Court declined to hear cases involving state gun restrictions, a police dog’s drug sniff, Ghislaine Maxwell’s prosecution, and Laura Loomer’s lawsuit against social media platforms. It also denied rehearing in a challenge to the transfer of land Native Americans consider sacred. The justices requested the federal government’s views in three other cases involving nuclear safety regulations, trademark law, and arbitration.
A Harvard Business School study found that several AI companions use tactics to keep conversations from ending.

Turtle Trading is a trend-following strategy developed by Richard Dennis and William Eckhardt during a 1983 experiment testing whether novices could learn to trade. Fourteen recruits were trained, and many who followed the rules became successful. The strategy uses price breakouts to enter trades, volatility-based position sizing to manage risk, pyramiding to add to winning positions, and predetermined stops and exits. The passage says the approach remains relevant in clearly trending markets, though its backtests suggest lower performance since 2007 than in earlier periods. It also notes frequent false signals, prolonged drawdowns, and the difficulty of following the rules in practice.

Preliminary BC Coroners Service data recorded 1,422 suspected illicit drug overdose deaths in British Columbia in 2017, up 43% from 2016. Deaths were lower in the final four months than in the first eight, though officials warned against complacency. Fentanyl was detected in about 81% of 2017 deaths. Most deaths occurred indoors, often in private residences; about four in five people who died were male. Vancouver had the most deaths among townships, with 358. No deaths occurred at supervised consumption or overdose prevention sites.

The study tested mixtures of mangosteen peel and grass jelly leaf dyes in dye-sensitized solar cells. Blending the dyes broadened light absorption, and the 1:3 mangosteen-to-grass-jelly ratio achieved the highest reported efficiency, 3.50%, compared with 2.75% and 2.12% for the individual dyes. Grass-jelly-rich mixtures also retained more efficiency over ten cycles, though long-term stability remains a focus for future work.

Luca Speight, 18, received the Outstanding Achievement Award and was named Isle of Wight College Student of the Year 2018. After a life-threatening illness kept him away for three months, the Catering and Hospitality student caught up with his work and excelled in his placement. He thanked his tutors, classmates, family and friends for their support.

The ADS868xW family comprises 16-bit SAR ADC devices with an integrated analog front end, antialiasing filter, ADC driver, and buffered voltage reference. The devices support single-ended and differential inputs across bipolar and unipolar ranges, with straight-binary output. They use a 4.096V internal reference by default or an external reference selected through a register.

Programmable input alarms and fixed AVDD alarms monitor voltage limits. A multiSPI interface supports standard SPI, single- or dual-output data, source-synchronous transfers, and daisy-chained devices. Configuration registers control input ranges, alarms, data output, reset behavior, and low-power NAP and power-down modes. The passage also describes reference and supply decoupling, PCB layout recommendations, and an eight-channel industrial input-module example using an ADS8681W with an external multiplexer.

The study uses a 225-agent urban migration simulation to examine how LLM agents balance personal and collective welfare. It identifies “Adaptive Egoists,” whose initially self-interested behavior can become more altruistic through a public message board, and “Altruistic Optimizers,” which prioritize collective welfare even without one. The authors argue that choosing an LLM for social simulation also means choosing the social behavior it represents. They note that the model simplifies migration and uses homogeneous agents, and propose human-participant comparisons and simulations with more diverse profiles.

Depoe Bay, Oregon, is preparing for large crowds when the Aug. 21 total solar eclipse first reaches land nearby before crossing 14 states. Hotels and campgrounds are sold out, but officials do not know how many visitors to expect. Drawing on disaster planning, the town has arranged extra restrooms, trash cans, protective glasses and fire staffing. Officials are also preparing for traffic gridlock on the town’s only road and increased boating at its small harbor.

Figma shares rose 7% Monday after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman demonstrated how ChatGPT users could ask Figma to turn a sketch into a diagram. Shares climbed as much as 16% during the session. OpenAI plans to review third-party app submissions later in 2025 and develop ways to monetize integrations.

Benjamin David Sherwood of Wisconsin was sentenced in Houston to 11 years in prison after pleading guilty to traveling across state lines and enticing a minor for sexual contact. Federal agents arrested him in 2017 after he traveled to meet a child who was part of an undercover operation. He will remain under lifelong supervision and register as a sex offender.

BMW and Brilliance Automotive launched the China-only 1 Series sedan in July 2016. BMW has not decided whether to bring it to India, where it would compete with the Mercedes-Benz CLA and Audi A3 sedans. The front-wheel-drive car measures 4,456 mm long and uses the UKL1 platform. Potential Indian versions include petrol and diesel engines.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPUs and related technologies. RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move lossless decompression from the CPU to the GPU, addressing storage bottlenecks in games and other data-intensive work. The A40 targets data-center visual computing and virtualized workloads, while the RTX A6000 targets professional workstations; both support configurations with up to 96GB of combined GPU memory through NVLink.

Ampere GPUs support high-resolution displays, HDMI 2.1, hardware video decoding through NVDEC—including AV1—and encoding through NVENC. The passage also outlines improvements to shading, ray tracing, AI processing, and memory performance, plus error detection and replay for GDDR6X memory overclocking. It concludes with product specifications, performance-test references, and legal notices.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2018 reports quarterly revenue of $26.8 billion and net income of $7.4 billion, up from $23.2 billion and $5.5 billion a year earlier. Nine-month revenue rose to $80.3 billion, while net income fell to $7.7 billion, primarily reflecting an estimated $13.8 billion charge related to U.S. tax legislation. At March 31, Microsoft held $132.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments. It repurchased $3.1 billion of shares during the quarter.

The Portland Thorns enter the NWSL playoffs seeking a championship after last season’s home semifinal loss. Portland, which finished second this year, hosts the third-place Orlando Pride on Saturday. The Supporters’ Shield-winning North Carolina Courage hosts the Chicago Red Stars on Sunday; the winners meet October 14 in Orlando. Pride midfielder Camila is out with a knee injury. In the league’s fifth season, Sky Blue’s Sam Kerr set a scoring record with 17 goals, and a new national broadcast deal will bring both semifinals to Lifetime.

Forecasts call for 7.5 inches of rain in the Feather River basin over 10 days, less than the 13.6 inches during the storm that damaged Oroville Dam’s spillways. Colder, more gradual precipitation is expected to produce less runoff. Officials are draining the reservoir, which stood about 15 feet below the emergency spillway Tuesday. A meteorologist said the lake should keep falling, but warned that sudden warm weather could melt the record snowpack and increase inflows.

Amazon’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2017, reports net sales of $35.7 billion, up 23% from a year earlier, and net income of $724 million, up from $513 million. Operating income fell to $1.0 billion from $1.1 billion. AWS operating income rose to $890 million, while the International operating loss widened to $481 million. Cash used in operating activities was $1.6 billion for the quarter; operating cash flow for the trailing twelve months was $17.6 billion. Amazon agreed to acquire Souq Group for $580 million in cash, subject to adjustments. For the second quarter, it forecast sales of $35.25 billion to $37.75 billion.

Schmidt Sciences will fund four remotely piloted boats to collect data in the Southern Ocean over five years, including during winter and beyond commercial shipping routes. The project aims to improve understanding of how the ocean around Antarctica absorbs carbon dioxide, a process scientists struggle to measure because of harsh conditions and limited observations. The boats will measure CO2 in the water, use machine learning to guide their routes, and make their data public. The project is part of a $45 million Schmidt Sciences program studying the global carbon cycle. It comes as proposed federal cuts threaten US climate research funding.

Phuket Governor Norraphat Plodthong ordered lifeguards back on beach patrol by April 1, according to Thailand’s National News Bureau. Local administrations were told to cover beaches in Muang Phuket and Kathu, while a procured company would cover Thalang. Offices lacking funds could request PPAO support, despite the governor’s earlier statement that the PPAO would no longer be involved. The report did not explain the change.

The lecture explains how the LSZ theorem obtains scattering amplitudes from on-shell correlation functions by retaining connected diagrams and removing external propagators. Corrections confined to external legs are accounted for by a constant Z, which does not contribute at leading order.

It then introduces the Dirac equation as a first-order candidate for describing relativistic fermions. Requiring its square to yield the Klein–Gordon equation leads to conditions on matrices that require a four-component spinor for massive particles. The corresponding gamma matrices satisfy the Clifford algebra; representations related by a change of basis are physically equivalent. Massless particles can instead be described with two-component spinors. The lecture ends by reviewing Lorentz covariance for a scalar field, leaving the Dirac equation’s covariance for the next lecture.

Lab experiments show that closely packed microbubbles of methane and air in water can produce tiny electrical sparks. Researchers suggest the sparks might ignite swamp gas and help explain will-o’-the-wisps, but other chemists caution that the underwater experiment differs from the conditions where the lights appear. The sparks could also help trigger chemical reactions or break down pollutants.

In a daisy chain, all devices share host-controlled CONVST/CS and SCLK signals, while each device’s SDO-0 connects to the next device’s SDI. The host programs identical configurations and sets SDO_CTL_REG bits 7–0 to 00h. Devices sample inputs on the CONVST/CS rising edge; the host receives data from the last device first. An optimal transfer frame has 32 × N SCLK capture edges; shorter frames cause erroneous configuration.

Solawave’s 4-in-1 Renewal Wand is on sale for a little over $100 during Prime Day. It targets specific areas with 630-nm red light, warmth, and vibration, but requires three minutes of manual use. WIRED staffers reported skin-tightening results, particularly around the eyes. Solawave’s face mask is also on sale for $227.

The passage describes AGESA procedures for establishing and removing a pre-memory stack, creating and initializing parameter structures, and querying processor and memory information. Stack setup uses cache before main memory is available and must run on all processor cores; stack removal disables cache-as-RAM mode after the stack has moved to main memory. AmdCreateStruct allocates storage by a selected method and initializes it with defaults. Other procedures return DIMM data-eye results, processor-core APIC addresses, pre-memory execution-cache size, processor-die PCI addresses, the current core’s socket, die and core identifiers, and the DIMM and location within it associated with a memory address. Most of these services require an established stack.

On February 10, 2016, Amazon elected Wendell P. Weeks to its board and Audit Committee, granting him 1,365 restricted stock units. The board approved a two-year leave for Diego Piacentini beginning in August 2016; Russ Grandinetti will assume responsibility for the international consumer business. The board also authorized up to $5 billion in share repurchases, replacing a $2 billion authorization from 2010.

EUR/USD is forming a bearish channel, though downside momentum may be slowing; a break above resistance would invalidate its wave 3 outlook. GBP/USD is testing triangle resistance, with a possible breakout or decline toward 1.05. USD/JPY’s bull flag suggests potential gains, while a support break indicates a possible larger retracement.

Natalie Grabow, 80, became the oldest woman to finish the Kona Ironman World Championship, completing it in 16 hours, 45 minutes, and 26 seconds. She learned to swim at 59 and began competing in triathlons at 60. To prepare, she works out for about two hours daily for months and eats a varied diet without restrictions. She plans to keep competing for as long as she can.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPUs and their gaming, professional, and data-center features. RTX IO works with Microsoft DirectStorage to move compressed data from SSD storage to the GPU for decompression, reducing CPU work and improving loading performance. Ampere GPUs offer advances in shading, ray tracing, AI processing, display support, and hardware video decoding and encoding, including AV1 decoding. The A40 targets data-center visual computing, while the RTX A6000 targets professional workstations; both support large datasets and can combine GPU memory through NVLink. The passage also outlines GeForce RTX 3090 and 3070 specifications and Error Detection and Replay for GDDR6X memory overclocking. NVIDIA closes with product-use limitations and warranty disclaimers.

The President urges Congress to modernize conservation laws while allowing responsible development of public resources. He calls for validating existing land withdrawals, classifying public lands, separating mineral rights from agricultural land, and leasing mineral deposits and water-power sites under conditions designed to prevent monopolies. He also emphasizes soil conservation, scientific forestry, and reforestation.

To finish irrigation projects already begun and aid settlers awaiting water, he recommends authorizing up to $30 million in bonds. For inland waterways, he urges funding planned improvements to the Ohio, upper Mississippi, and Missouri rivers. He asks Congress to act promptly rather than wait for an investigation into the Interior Department and Forest Service.

The passage specifies the Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocol for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests, whose register state is protected from the hypervisor. It describes how guests selectively share state for non-automatic exits, negotiate protocol versions, establish a shared GHCB page, and use MSR and VMGEXIT requests. It also covers feature advertisement, page-state changes, SNP firmware requests, AP creation and booting, interrupt handling, trusted I/O, and Secure AVIC. For restricted injection, it defines a shared #HV doorbell page and the host and guest behavior for presenting interrupts, acknowledging them, and completing end-of-interrupt cycles.

Lenovo unveiled the limited-edition ThinkPad 25, a T470-based laptop styled after the 1992 ThinkPad 700C. It pairs retro features, including a seven-row keyboard and red TrackPoint, with modern hardware. Available in limited quantities in select countries, it starts at $1,899.

Consumer confidence measures consumers’ optimism about the economy and can signal changes in spending. The passage describes monthly confidence surveys from the Conference Board and the University of Michigan, but its stock-market backtests use OECD data for the United States. From 1993 over 28 years, investing in the S&P 500 only when confidence exceeded its 12-month average turned $10,000 into $99,000, versus $159,000 for buy-and-hold. The strategy was invested 55% of the time and had a lower maximum drawdown. Investing only when confidence was below that average turned $10,000 into $15,000.

The passage describes NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPUs for data centers, workstations, gaming and video processing. The A40 supports visual computing and virtualized workloads, with 48GB of memory expandable to 96GB through NVLink. Ampere GPUs add improved ray tracing, AI and FP32 performance, high-resolution display support, hardware AV1 decoding and dedicated video encoding. It also covers the RTX A6000 workstation GPU, GeForce RTX 30-series models, GDDR6X memory, RTX IO and error detection and replay for memory overclocking. The passage concludes with product specifications, performance-test notes and legal disclaimers.

COPD is caused almost exclusively by smoking and can cause chronic coughing and shortness of breath. Doctors assess smoking history and use breathing tests to diagnose it. There is no cure, but inhalers, oxygen and pulmonary rehabilitation can help manage symptoms. Quitting smoking can prevent COPD and slow its progression.

First-principles calculations of Mn3Sn(01¯10)/MgO(110)/Mn3Sn magnetic tunnel junctions find a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio exceeding 1000% with a sufficiently thick MgO barrier. The effect arises from momentum-dependent spin polarization in Mn3Sn and electron filtering by MgO. The studied orientation is suitable for electrical switching of Mn3Sn’s magnetic configuration.

Molecular dynamics commonly calculates thermal conductivity using Green–Kubo or non-equilibrium methods, both of which rely on heat flux. Existing LAMMPS heat-flux calculations can be incorrect for many-body potentials, while heat-current and spectral-decomposition implementations have largely been limited to pairwise interactions. This work implements formulas for heat flux through a control volume and heat current across a control surface, including its spectral decomposition, for arbitrary many-body potentials in LAMMPS. It describes comparative tests using Tersoff and Stillinger–Weber potentials and spectral calculations for graphene and MoS₂.

A qualitative study interviewed 14 sports-science lecturers in Turkey about distance education during COVID-19. They cited flexibility, access to resources and lower costs as benefits, but reported motivation, communication, internet access and assessment problems. Practical sports lessons were particularly difficult to deliver. Participants also raised concerns about how the transition was managed. The study recommends designing distance education around course goals and student access, protecting personal data and conducting further research.

Jeff Bezos has proposed orbital data centres to meet growing cloud and AI computing demand while reducing pressure on Earth’s land, energy and cooling resources. The idea remains speculative: radiation, cooling, communications, launch costs and maintenance pose major hurdles.

A study found that barn owls can distinguish a moving target from shifting background dots by grouping elements that move in the same direction, a visual-processing ability previously tested only in primates. The owls found targets more easily when the background dots moved uniformly rather than in scattered directions. Activity in the ocular tectum varied with the dots’ movement, suggesting this brain area helps perform the task.
Stronger-than-expected US job growth and wage gains raised expectations of Federal Reserve interest rate hikes on Friday, lifting the dollar and bond yields while stocks fell.

Gold edged lower on Friday as the dollar strengthened against the euro ahead of U.S. payrolls data, which investors were watching for clues about interest-rate increases. Spot gold fell 0.3 percent to $1,345.22 an ounce. The Federal Reserve had held rates steady this week but signaled further gradual increases. Palladium was on track for its biggest weekly drop since early September.

Lifeline Fiji says suicide remains a taboo subject despite 627 suicides and 694 attempted suicides recorded in Fiji from 2011 to March this year. Program director Jeremiah Merekula called for greater awareness of emotional wellbeing and available support. Lifeline Fiji is working with children and parents and offers a 24/7 helpline at 132454.

Clark County Schools Superintendent Pat Skorkowsky retired after five years in the role and 30 years in the district. He cited a rise in the graduation rate from 60 to 83 percent and the addition of more than 10,000 magnet-school seats. Facing a $60 million budget shortfall, he urged incoming superintendent Dr. Jesus Jara and the school board to address funding with lawmakers. He also called for more campus mental health professionals and advised Jara to listen to the community.

The passage describes a social-network location-sharing system that predicts a user’s destination by comparing their current trajectory with historical locations and recurring routes. With user authorization, it can show friends the presumed destination on a map alongside the user’s avatar and an estimated arrival time. The system updates predictions as new location data arrives and may use a recurring route to estimate the user’s position when updates stop.

Vale of Glamorgan Brewery has applied to open the Radyr Tap micropub in a vacant Station Road unit. Radyr has had no pub since the Radyr Arms closed in 2003. The proposed venue would serve local beers, other drinks and snacks. A consultation runs until June 19 before Cardiff council makes a decision.

At RSA Conference 2017, Intel Security’s Chris Young warned that manipulated data can distort decisions and cause economic losses. He also said insecure home networks and internet-of-things devices pose risks to corporate networks as more people work from home.

Microsoft President Brad Smith urged technology companies to cooperate as a “digital Switzerland,” defending customers and civilians rather than conducting attacks. He called for international agreements protecting private and civil infrastructure, government disclosure of software vulnerabilities, and an independent body to monitor and attribute nation-state cyberattacks.

MIT has become the first of nine universities to publicly reject the Trump administration’s proposed higher education compact, which offers preferential federal funding in exchange for campus changes. President Sally Kornbluth said some demands would restrict free expression and institutional independence, and conflicted with MIT’s view that funding should be based on merit. Most other invited universities are still reviewing the proposal, while Texas officials have expressed interest. MIT’s decision drew praise from academics and lawmakers; some Trump-aligned figures hinted at possible retaliation.

A jury at Leicester Crown Court heard allegations that spiritual healer Komar Uddin sexually assaulted and twice raped a 19-year-old woman during a ritual at her family home in 2015. The woman said she was frightened, initially thought his actions were part of the treatment, and told her family after he left. Prosecutors said an internal swab contained Uddin’s DNA. Uddin denies all charges, and his defence suggested the woman had initiated sexual contact, which she denied. The trial continues.

The passage describes MSPM0G microcontrollers with an 80 MHz ARM Cortex-M0+ CPU and five power modes, from RUN to SHUTDOWN. It outlines clock and power management, DMA, event routing, flash and SRAM, GPIO, and analog functions including ADCs, a DAC, comparators, and a temperature sensor. It also covers security features, serial interfaces, timers, watchdogs, debugging, and a UART or I2C bootloader. Application guidance addresses supply decoupling, reset circuitry, and required external components. The document concludes with development resources, revision history, packaging information, and TI disclaimers.

Prosecutors released three cellphone videos in which Nikolas Cruz described plans to shoot students at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School and spoke about his loneliness and anger. The Feb. 14 attack killed 17 people and injured 17. Cruz faces 17 murder and 17 attempted-murder charges. His lawyers say he would plead guilty if guaranteed life without parole, but prosecutors have not waived the death penalty. The videos became public through Florida’s pretrial evidence rules.

Amazon’s 2020 Form 10-K describes three operating segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services. For 2020, it reports net sales of $386.1 billion, operating income of $22.9 billion, and net income of $21.3 billion. Operating cash flow was $66.1 billion, and cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $84.4 billion at year-end. Amazon hired over 400,000 employees from February 2020 to expand fulfillment capacity and incurred more than $11.5 billion in COVID-19-related costs during the year. The filing discusses risks including competition, international regulation, fulfillment capacity, cybersecurity, litigation, and taxes.

The passage calls for 1,000 more naval officers, larger classes at Annapolis, and retirement and promotion measures to ease the strain on officers and maintain an efficient navy despite the absence of an immediate foreign threat. It reports record growth in postal receipts and urges continued expansion of rural free delivery, citing increased receipts and benefits to farmers. It also supports nationally aided irrigation in the far West, stronger forest protection, and measures to stop the slaughter of wildlife on forest reserves.

Researchers found that blocking the protein Ant2 reprogrammed T cells’ energy use, improving their stamina, replication and ability to attack tumors in mice. The effect could be triggered genetically or with drugs, but further studies and clinical trials are needed.

Michael T. Klare argues that Trump is pursuing a world order centered on fossil fuels, favoring closer ties with Saudi Arabia and Russia while distancing the United States from renewable-energy supporters in Europe and China. He cites Trump’s Saudi arms deal, criticism of NATO, withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement, and efforts to expand domestic fossil-fuel production. Klare says a U.S.–Saudi–Russian alliance would wield substantial energy power, but disputes over Syria and Iran, along with controversy over Russian election meddling, pose obstacles.

Facebook took more than two hours to remove videos posted by suspect Steve Stephens of Robert Godwin’s shooting death. Immigrant rights activist Hugo Castro disappeared in Mexico after requesting help on Facebook Live. In Georgia, Democrats hope Jon Ossoff can win a long-held Republican House seat amid opposition to Trump.

A survey of 304 medical students at four Belgian universities found limited knowledge and exposure to global surgery despite strong interest: 24.7% reported prior exposure, 75.3% wanted more, and about 95% considered it relevant. Students preferred teaching, events and clinical internships for further exposure. Reported career barriers included personal responsibilities, language, unclear career paths, finances and limited mentorship. The authors recommend pre-clinical seminars and equitable international internships, while noting that the nonrandom sample limits generalizability.

Paul Ehrlich’s 1968 depiction of crowded Delhi helped fuel fears of overpopulation, but demographer Jack Caldwell argued that similar crowding existed in Western cities and questioned whether Ehrlich’s reaction reflected who he saw. The passage argues that cities tend to reduce population growth because urban residents have fewer children than rural residents. Urban populations grow largely through migration from rural areas. Yet cities also consume disproportionate resources: although they house half the world’s population, they use three-quarters of the materials taken from the planet.

A March 2018 test of 124 VPN and proxy providers reported that 20 leaked users’ real IP addresses through WebRTC, while 101 kept them hidden. The passage lists affected providers, links to leak-testing tools, and suggests disabling WebRTC or using a browser add-on if a leak is found. It also lists VPN services reported to protect users’ IP addresses.

Caterpillar kept its quarterly dividend at $0.77 per share, its seventh consecutive flat payout.
